label: Progressive Democrats
description: Most liberal profile in the sample: expansive on social liberty and equality, justice-leaning rather than punitive on order, and the only group positive on immigration inclusion. Concentrated in modern and urban seats; shows the lowest overperformance against the fixed 2018-24 reference.
evidence: 56 people; social liberty +0.81 (n=50), immigration +1.01 (n=20), order/justice -0.71 (n=48); mean cycle WAR 4.10 (SE 2.02)

label: Mainstream statehouse Democrats
description: The roll-call-rich legislative core, mostly serving 2006-2014. Strongly supportive of material support and environmental protection and reform-minded on institutions, while culturally restrictive on immigration and mixed on labor questions.
evidence: 98 people; 13,627 legislative records; material support +0.94 (n=95), environment +0.26 (n=66), immigration -0.42 (n=44); mean cycle WAR 25.57 (SE 2.20)

label: Institutional traditionalists
description: Defined mainly by opposition to institutional and ethics reform and by distance from organized labor. Thin and uneven evidence, drawn from the 2002 and 2022 cohorts, and the least electorally observed group: 55% of its candidate-cycles have no contested general election.
evidence: 30 people; institutional reform -1.31 (n=23), labor -0.78 (n=22); no member observed on immigration; mean cycle WAR 18.77 (SE 5.11)

label: Rural labor Democrats
description: Pro-labor and reform-minded but sceptical of environmental regulation and restrictive on immigration; largely the 1990s and 2000s rural cohort. The most electorally observed group, with only 17% of candidate-cycles unscored.
evidence: 51 people; labor +0.49 (n=42), environment -0.66 (n=50), immigration -0.47 (n=9); mean cycle WAR 21.80 (SE 2.79)

label: Old-guard conservative Democrats
description: The 1990s conservative Democratic profile: market-leaning on the role of government and restrictive on social liberty, while retaining support for material spending. Highest measured overperformance against the modern reference model, which is partly by construction for pre-2016 cycles.
evidence: 27 people; market/government -0.94 (n=25), social liberty -0.90 (n=23); mean cycle WAR 30.97 (SE 3.71)
